title: External HTTP/3 Peer Harness Architecture
purpose: Define an advisory Docker Compose based HTTP/3 peer harness outside the upstream QUIC interop runner.
design_summary: The harness uses Docker Compose as the target inventory and small runner scripts as the execution surface. The scripts create deterministic fixture files, generate short-lived TLS materials, start the Incursa HTTP/3 server, execute wired client/server cells, and emit one JSONL row per target/scenario. The parser converts JSONL into a Markdown matrix. Peer cells that require unpinned external command syntax or specialized scenario endpoints are reported as `skip` until wired, keeping evidence honest while still showing the full desired matrix. A skipped row is not support evidence.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The harness must work from Windows PowerShell and POSIX shells.
The harness must keep generated artifacts under `.artifacts/http3-external` by default.
The checked-in Compose file must list optional peer images without requiring all of them to run for a plan or partial matrix.
The report parser must preserve pass, fail, and skip states distinctly.
The harness must not mutate upstream quic-interop-runner behavior.
risks: External images change over time; the first slice therefore keeps image names configurable through environment variables.
Different peer tools expose different HTTP/3 client/server command lines; skipped rows avoid pretending command wiring is complete before it is proven.
